_comment: Hand-written prose for the per-level manuals. Everything countable (lesson titles, goals, grammar focus, vocabulary, Hub themes/words/idioms/grammar topics, story parts, game name) is read from the live data by gen_manuals.py — never type numbers here.

pre-a.name: First Words
pre-a.cover_quote: Hi! I'm Lumi. Let's learn our very first English words together!
pre-a.intro: The very beginning of the journey: first greetings, the alphabet, numbers, colors, family, and everyday things -- all through play, songs, and repetition, no reading required.
outcomes: Say hello and goodbye, and their own name
Recognize and say all 26 letters of the alphabet
Count from zero to ten
Name basic colors
Name family members and parts of the body
Name common animals, foods, toys, and school things
Say simple action words and how they feel
pre-a.grammar_blurb: Vocabulary and functional language only -- formal grammar begins in Level 3. At this age, the goal is confident first words and sounds, not sentence structure.
pre-a.writing: At this age, before reading is even required, the task is simple and physical -- tracing and copying each word by hand, then drawing a picture for it. This builds letter formation and muscle memory long before your child is asked to write a sentence, and gives them a non-verbal way to show they understood a word.
pre-a.game_desc: A letter-and-listening game built around the alphabet your child is currently learning: Lumi names a specific word, and your child finds it among two or three other words that start with the very same letter -- a real test of listening past the first sound, not just picture-matching.
game_steps: Lumi shows a letter your child has already learned, and asks for one specific word that starts with it (for example, "Find 'nine'!"). Every picture shown genuinely starts with that same letter, so your child has to listen for the whole word, not just the first sound.
The letters used only ever come from lessons your child has already completed -- nothing shows up before it's been taught.
A few rounds also ask about a word or short sentence from the current lesson itself, mixing in vocabulary alongside the alphabet practice.
Each correct answer earns a star; by the final round, all six stars are filled in.

level1.name: About Me
level1.cover_quote: Welcome to Level 1! I'm Omar -- let's build real sentences together.
level1.intro: Real sentences begin here: describing things, saying what your child likes and doesn't like, and talking about their home, clothes, and abilities.
outcomes: Form simple sentences with "this is..." / "I am..."
Describe size ("big", "small") and count to 20
Say what they like and don't like
Name rooms, furniture, and clothes
Talk about the weather and days of the week
Use prepositions like "in", "on", and "under"
Describe shapes and simple opposites
Say what they can and can't do
level1.grammar_blurb: A new sentence pattern in nearly every lesson -- "this is", "I like", "I can", "where is" -- used in real sentences from day one. Formal grammar rules and the Grammar Hub begin in Level 3.
level1.writing: At this level, the task is still tracing and copying each word by hand, then drawing a picture for it. This continues building letter formation and muscle memory before sentence-writing begins at Level 3, and gives your child a non-verbal way to show they understood a word.
level1.game_desc: A phonics-focused listening game: Lumi says a specific word built from letter sounds your child has already learned, and they find it among other words from that same phonics group -- with a treehouse piece added for every correct answer.
game_steps: Lumi says a specific word (for example, "egg") built from phonics sounds your child has already covered in this level, and shows a few labeled pictures.
Your child taps the picture whose word matches what they heard -- since the sounds are still fresh, this trains real letter-sound recognition, not just picture memory.
A few rounds also use this lesson's own vocabulary and example sentences, so words and simple sentence patterns get practiced too.
Each correct answer adds a new piece to the treehouse -- a wall, a roof, a ladder -- until it's fully built and ready to celebrate.

level2.name: My World
level2.cover_quote: Hi, I'm Sara! Ready to explore school, family, and daily life with me?
level2.intro: The world widens here: extended family, telling time, daily routines morning and night, and the first steps into pointing things out with this/that/these/those.
outcomes: Greet people and introduce themselves properly
Name extended family (aunt, uncle, cousin)
Use he/she and possessives (my, your, his, her, our, their)
Follow classroom commands and count to 100
Name the months and tell the time
Describe their daily morning and evening routine
Point things out with this/that/these/those
Make plurals correctly (s/es)
level2.grammar_blurb: Possessives and he/she, classroom commands, telling time, this/that/these/those and plurals -- each introduced through the lesson's own sentences and practiced in class. The Grammar Hub with formal rules opens in Level 3.
level2.writing: Your child still traces and copies each word by hand, but the second task has changed -- instead of drawing, it's now "Talk About It", an open question like "Can you use 'hello' in your own sentence?" This is a deliberate bridge toward Level 3, where full sentence-writing begins, easing your child from copying words into thinking in them.
level2.game_desc: A calendar-book theme built around this level's real phonics focus: Lumi says a specific word from the letter sounds your child has already learned, and each correct answer reveals a new month's page, building a full year of the calendar one page at a time.
game_steps: Lumi says a specific word built from phonics sounds your child has already covered in this level, and three labeled pictures appear.
Your child taps the picture whose word matches what they heard, reinforcing the letter sounds behind it, not just the picture. A wrong tap costs nothing -- they simply try another option.
A few rounds also use this lesson's own vocabulary and example sentences, covering words and simple sentences too.
A correct answer reveals the next month on the calendar page; by the end of all six rounds, a good run earns a special "Wonderful!" celebration as the book fills up.

level3.name: Everyday Life
level3.cover_quote: I've grown up a bit! Welcome to the Crew -- real grammar starts now.
level3.intro: Real grammar begins here, and the full character cast joins in: Omar, Sara, Noor, Ziad, and Hamad. Conversations get longer, opinions get shared, and your child starts using English the way friends actually talk to each other.
outcomes: Talk about what friends do together (Present Simple)
Describe their room with "there is / there are"
Say what they can and can't do
Ask and answer questions about routines and skills
Talk about ongoing actions ("right now")
Follow classroom rules and school conversations
Read and understand a short story
level3.grammar_blurb: Present Simple, there is/are, can/can't, present continuous, and more -- one clear grammar point per lesson, each with its own rule page in the Grammar Hub, building toward real connected conversation.
level3.writing: This is where the task changes for good. Instead of drawing or answering an open question, your child now writes three original sentences using that day's real grammar pattern -- for example, Present Simple in Lesson 1. This is production, not recognition: applying the rule your child just learned, not just picking the right answer on screen.
level3.game_desc: A group-chat simulation with the full character cast, mixing four kinds of rounds: translating a word, describing a shared photo, spelling a word letter by letter, and understanding a full sentence.
game_steps: Translate rounds: a crew member asks how to say an Arabic word in English -- tap the right reply, or spell it back letter by letter using scrambled tiles.
Caption rounds: a crew member shares a photo and asks what's happening -- your child picks which of the lesson's own real sentences actually describes it.
Meaning rounds: a crew member sends a full English sentence and asks what it means -- your child picks the matching Arabic translation, practicing whole-sentence understanding.

Every playthrough mixes all four round types, and a short answer streak gets a hype message from the crew. Correct answers appear as real sent messages, building an actual conversation as the game goes on.

level4.name: Smart Choices
level4.cover_quote: Hey, I'm Ziad! Time to talk money, routines, and smart decisions.
level4.intro: Everyday decision-making in English: routines, money, requests, and advice -- the language your child needs to navigate real choices, not just describe the world around them.
outcomes: Describe routines with frequency words (always, never, how often)
Talk about sequence (before and after)
Ask politely and talk about possessions
Ask about prices and talk about saving money
Make polite requests ("I'd like...")
Give and receive advice ("you should")
Talk about future plans and the wider world
level4.grammar_blurb: Frequency adverbs, possessives, requests with "I'd like", modals like "should" -- one grammar point per lesson with its own Grammar Hub rule page, building toward real decision-making conversation.
level4.writing: Your child continues writing three original sentences using that day's real grammar pattern -- for example, Present Simple Questions in Lesson 1. This is production, not recognition: applying the rule just learned, in a sentence your child builds themselves, not one picked from a list.
level4.game_desc: A shopping-list budgeting game that also practices real conversation: most rounds have your child "buy" items from an Arabic shopping list, and a couple of rounds ask what comes next in a real chat between friends.
game_steps: Shopping rounds: an Arabic shopping list appears with priced market stalls -- your child listens for the word Lumi says, then taps the matching stall to "buy" it. A correct purchase adds it to a running receipt and deducts its price; a wrong tap costs nothing, and by the end the receipt shows everything bought plus coins left over.
Conversation rounds: two lines of a real back-and-forth chat appear, and your child picks what really comes next from three options -- genuine dialogue practice, not just vocabulary.

level5.name: Telling My Story
level5.cover_quote: Hi, I'm Noor! Get ready to tell real stories about your own life.
level5.intro: The past tense arrives here: what happened, when, and why. Your child moves from describing the present to genuinely telling stories -- their weekend, a trip, a party, a mistake -- in connected, real narrative.
outcomes: Talk about what happened yesterday or last weekend
Ask and answer questions in the past ("Did you...?")
Describe how something was and why it happened
Tell a story with sequence ("and then...")
Describe what was happening at a specific moment
Talk about a trip, a party, or a memorable day
Interview someone and recap a story
level5.grammar_blurb: Past simple, past questions, past continuous, and connecting words -- one grammar point per lesson with its own Grammar Hub rule page, building toward real storytelling.
level5.writing: Your child writes three original sentences using that day's real grammar pattern -- for example, Past Simple regular verbs in Lesson 1. Since this level's whole focus is telling real stories about the past, this is where your child actually practices narrating their own weekend, not just recognizing past-tense forms on screen.
level5.game_desc: A detective mystery theme covering three kinds of clues: finding the right meaning of a word, judging whether a witness got a translation right, and figuring out what was really said next in an overheard conversation.
game_steps: Find the evidence: an Arabic word or phrase is shown with three English options -- tap the one that matches its meaning.
Verify the clue: a witness claims an Arabic phrase means a certain English word -- your child judges True or False.

Witness testimony: two lines of a real overheard conversation are shown, and your child figures out what was really said next from three options. Every confirmed answer gets pinned to the case file as evidence; by the end, the full case file is revealed -- "mystery solved!"

level6.name: Looking Ahead
level6.cover_quote: Welcome, I'm Hamad! Let's talk about the future -- plans, hopes, and predictions.
level6.intro: The final level of the journey: the future tense, predictions, comparisons, and real debate. Your child finishes here able to plan, predict, compare, and argue a point of view in English.
outcomes: Talk about future plans and predictions ("will", "going to")
Describe what was happening while something else occurred
Talk about rules, duties, and obligations
Make comparisons ("even better", "which is better?")
Discuss multitasking and daily habits
Join a class debate and defend an opinion
Compare cultures and traditions
level6.grammar_blurb: Future forms, past continuous, modals of obligation, and comparatives -- one grammar point per lesson with its own Grammar Hub rule page, capping off the full 7-level grammar progression.
level6.writing: Your child writes three original sentences using that day's real grammar pattern -- for example, "going to" for future plans in Lesson 1. Fittingly for this level's own focus on looking ahead, this is where your child practices actually stating their own real plans and predictions, not just recognizing the future tense on screen.
level6.game_desc: A fortune-telling theme fitting Level 6's future-focused lessons, covering three kinds of visions: reading a word's meaning, judging a prediction, and seeing what happens next in a real conversation.
game_steps: Read the crystal ball: an Arabic word appears inside the glowing ball with three English options -- tap the correct meaning.
Judge the prediction: the ball shows a claimed Arabic-to-English match -- your child taps Correct or Wrong to judge it.

A vision unfolds: the ball "shows" two lines of a real conversation, and your child picks what really happens next from three options. Each correct answer across all three round types builds up a "power" meter that makes the ball glow brighter -- a fully-charged meter by the end means "the future looks bright!"

flashcards_young: Every card shows the picture and English word on one side and the Arabic translation on the other. That means either parent can quiz their child at home, even without speaking English themselves -- a two-minute flip-through before bed is real, screen-free repetition that helps new words genuinely stick.
flashcards_teen: Every card shows the picture and English word on one side and the Arabic translation on the other. That means either parent can quiz their teen at home, even without speaking English themselves -- a quick flip-through is real, screen-free repetition that keeps vocabulary fresh alongside the grammar work.
